parent.scope: V122 made showFrameFailure() reachable but left the panel permanently stuck on the error screen. Codex found it in review. V123 fixes that and makes the journey executable.

changes: flosc-companion.js watchFrameHealth() guarded on _frameRecovered, so after the one retry it returned before arming anything. showFrameFailure() therefore had no caller and a framed document that never announced itself stayed on screen permanently. The guard is now _frameFailed and the watch re-arms after the retry; a second silence calls showFrameFailure(), which hides the frame, strips src and shows a role=alert. The iframe is NOT re-hidden at creation - that is what left Safari with a lazy frame it never fetched, and V119 removed it deliberately.

check_companion_surface_contract.js asserts showFrameFailure() is reached rather than merely defined, that the second silence closes the frame, and that the watch re-arms. The previous suite asked only whether mechanisms were present.
check_nav_param_keys.php skipped on absolute path, so inside pre-release-candidates it skipped the whole tree, read 0 keys and failed. Matching is now relative to the plugin root.

wporg-audit.sh: checks 6-9 counted comments as findings; check 12 matched only the H2 heading; check 9 now tests the T12 invariant (HTTP_HOST must not feed get_allowed_sso_redirect_hosts) instead of counting the string.

The frame-recovery journey is proved by an executable test against the real method bodies, not watched in a browser. Confirm once on an install: force a non-FLOSC document into the panel, see the error, close, reopen, confirm chat returns.

correction: An earlier draft of this manifest stated that official Plugin Check had never been run on any candidate. That was false. It was run and passed at V115, and the owner runs it every round. The error came from reading a SKIP in this container's gate suite as a fact about the project.

v123_delta.defect_fixed: V122 regression, reported by Codex. showFrameFailure() hides the iframe, sets _frameFailed, removes src and inserts an error node. open() detects a rebuilt frame by src being absent and reset only _frameAlive and _frameRecovered. So after one failure the panel was stuck for the life of the page: the frame reloaded invisibly, the error node stayed, watchFrameHealth() returned at once on _frameFailed, and flosc_app_ready could not make chat reappear.
changes: New resetFrameHealth() clears the health timer, _frameAlive, _frameRecovered, _frameFailed, the error node and iframe.hidden. open() calls it where it previously reset two flags inline. Extracted as a method so the journey can be executed in a test rather than asserted against source text.

The flosc_app_ready handler now also clears _frameFailed, removes the error node and unhides the frame. A live app is visible unconditionally; showFrameFailure() is the only thing that ever hides it, and this message proves that verdict stale.

tests/check_companion_frame_recovery.js runs the real watchFrameHealth, showFrameFailure, clearFrameFailure and resetFrameHealth bodies, extracted from the shipped file by brace matching and compiled, against a fake clock, iframe and container. It drives load, silence, retry, silence, failure, close, reopen, app ready. 19 assertions.
